title: Constant-target and constant-source tests for relative universal cones
statement:
Use the simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent transformations, spaces and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the relative universal diagrams and joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and the quasicategory and Kan-mapping-space assertions of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Let $p:D\to B$ be any functor of quasicategories, let $K$ be any small simplicial set, and let $q:K^{\triangleright}\to D$, with $f=q|_K$ and $x=q(*)$. Write $\alpha:f\to\Delta_Kx$ for the coherent cocone obtained by precomposition with $K\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}$, retaining the initial $K$-vertices labelled $0$ and sending the vertices labelled $1$ to the apex. Then $q$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if for every vertex $z$ of $D$ the following square of spaces is a homotopy pullback:
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
\operatorname{Map}_D(x,z)&\xrightarrow{u\mapsto\Delta_K(u)\alpha}&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(f,\Delta_Kz)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\operatorname{Map}_B(px,pz)&\xrightarrow{v\mapsto\Delta_K(v)(p\alpha)}&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(pf,\Delta_K(pz)).
\end{array}$$
Composition and commutativity here include their coherent homotopies. For a homotopy-commuting square, the path-pullback comparison sends a point to its two images together with the specified path between their images in the lower-right corner; this comparison must be a weak homotopy equivalence, and all higher simplices of the path data are retained. Equivalently, in the all-diagrams testing square defining a $p$-colimit diagram, it suffices to take the target diagram to be constant at each $z$ on $K^{\triangleright}$. The passage between these two tests is natural in $p$ and in restriction along any simplicial map $L\to K$, including the induced coherent cocones; the apex is unchanged by restriction. Dually, if $q:K^{\triangleleft}\to D$ has apex $x$ and boundary $f$, it is a $p$-limit diagram if and only if, for every vertex $z$ of $D$, the square with upper row
$$\operatorname{Map}_D(z,x)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(\Delta_Kz,f)$$
and lower row the corresponding square in $B$, induced by its coherent cone, is a homotopy pullback. Equivalently, only constant source test diagrams are needed. All objects lie in fixed sufficiently large universes. No fibration hypothesis on $p$ and no existence of any other limits or colimits is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, equivalence of conditions (2) and (3), and its colimit dual; apex form obtained from the constant-diagram test by restriction to the cone vertex (the cone-vertex inclusion is one-sided anodyne; restriction gives the constant-target mapping-space equivalence). Coherent cocones use 4.6.5.10. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; read online, archival source WANTED.

proof.text:
We prove the limit orientation first, because [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] states its varying-boundary formula for left cones. Write a left cone $q$ as $(x,f,\alpha:\Delta_Kx\to f)$ and an arbitrary source cone $t$ as $(z,g,\beta:\Delta_Kz\to g)$. Put
$$A_D=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(g,f),\quad C_D=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(\Delta_Kz,f),\quad M_D=\operatorname{Map}_D(z,x),$$
and define $A_B,C_B,M_B$ by applying $p$. The join-cone formula gives, naturally with the boundary projection,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleleft},D)}(t,q)\simeq A_D\times^h_{C_D}M_D.$$
Here the two maps are $a\mapsto a\beta$ and $u\mapsto\alpha\Delta_K(u)$; the path is the coherence of a map of cones. The same formula holds in $B$, and its naturality identifies postcomposition by $p$ with the map between these two path pullbacks. This is the varying-boundary formula, rather than the fixed-boundary cone-fiber formula. All six spaces are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus].

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, condition (2); mapping-space reformulation; agent proof using the existing varying-boundary join-cone mapping formula.

proof.text:
For $t$ constant at $z$, its boundary is $\Delta_Kz$ and $\beta$ is the identity. Thus $A_D=C_D$ and the first map into $C_D$ is the identity; the constant-path map
$$M_D\longrightarrow C_D\times^h_{C_D}M_D$$
is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], since an identity is a Kan fibration. This equivalence is over $C_D$, with the map $u\mapsto\alpha\Delta_K(u)$, and the same holds naturally in $B$. The invariance theorem [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] therefore identifies the constant-source all-diagrams square with the apex square $M_D\to C_D$ over $M_B\to C_B$. The comparison retains the coherence path and every higher simplex. In particular the all-diagrams condition of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] implies the displayed constant-source criterion, and testing only constant source diagrams is equivalent to testing this apex square.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, (2) implies (3), and apex identification; agent proof using the existing varying-boundary join-cone mapping formula.

proof.text:
Assume now that the apex square is a homotopy pullback for every $z$. Fix $t=(z,g,\beta)$ as in step 1. The assumption says
$$M_D\simeq C_D\times^h_{C_B}M_B.$$
Apply homotopy-pullback invariance [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to pull back this equivalence along $A_D\to C_D$. In the resulting iterated pullbacks one can compute by fibrations, as follows. Replace $M_B\to C_B$ by a weak equivalence followed by a Kan fibration $\widehat M_B\to C_B$, using [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The pullback $C_D\times_{C_B}\widehat M_B\to C_D$ is already a fibration. The same statement and [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] compute its homotopy pullbacks by strict pullbacks. Degreewise associativity now identifies both
$$A_D\times^h_{C_D}(C_D\times^h_{C_B}M_B)\quad\hbox{and}\quad A_D\times^h_{A_B}(A_B\times^h_{C_B}M_B)$$
with $A_D\times_{C_B}\widehat M_B$: the intermediate $C_D$ or $A_B$ coordinate is forced to be the image of the $A_D$ coordinate. For a specified commutation homotopy $H:Z\times\Delta^1\to W$ between $ru$ and $vs$, use [lem-coef-space-path-fibration-replacement] on $r:Y\to W$: the map $z\mapsto(u(z),H(z,-))$ lands in $E_r=Y\times_{W,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W)$ and its terminal evaluation is exactly $vs(z)$. Thus the square with top map to $E_r$ strictly commutes, and $Y\to E_r$ by constant paths is a weak equivalence. Apply this construction to the specified coherence squares before the fibration computations; projection back to $Y$ recovers the original maps and their specified paths. Strict invariance [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] and independence of replacement in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] then justify the same calculation for those coherent squares. In particular no strictly commuting invariance assertion is applied directly to a merely homotopy-commuting square. The identifications preserve the comparison induced by $p$. Together with step 1 this proves
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleleft},D)}(t,q)\simeq A_D\times^h_{A_B}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleleft},B)}(pt,pq).$$
This is exactly the all-diagrams square of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], for arbitrary $t$. Thus the constant-source criterion implies that $q$ is a $p$-limit diagram. No fibration hypothesis on $p$ has entered: only the auxiliary replacements of maps of Kan spaces were fibrations.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, (3) implies (2); explicit pullback argument; agent proof using the existing varying-boundary join-cone mapping formula.

proof.text:
We give the opposite construction explicitly to prove the colimit assertion. For an operator $a:[m]\to[n]$, write $\rho_n(i)=n-i$ and replace $a$ by $\rho_na\rho_m$. This operation preserves composition, squares to the identity, and carries horn $i$ to horn $n-i$. Hence it preserves quasicategories and Kan complexes. Reversing the two join blocks in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] gives $(K^{\triangleright})^{\mathrm{op}}\cong(K^{\mathrm{op}})^{\triangleleft}$; reversing product simplices gives $(\operatorname{Fun}(K,D))^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},D^{\mathrm{op}})$. Thus a cocone $f\to\Delta_Kx$ becomes a cone in $D^{\mathrm{op}}$.
For the arrow spaces $U$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], reversing the parameter simplex and exchanging the two interval endpoints gives the strict natural isomorphism $U_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}(z,x)\cong U_D(x,z)^{\mathrm{op}}$. The opposite on the right is essential. To compare a Kan complex $T$ with $T^{\mathrm{op}}$, use [lem-coef-subdivision-face-poset-calculus]: on the summand of $\sigma:\Delta^n\to T$, send a flag $(S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_k)$ to $(\rho_nS_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\rho_nS_k)$ in the reversed simplex. Since $\rho_na=(\rho_na\rho_m)\rho_m$, this respects the colimit relations and gives a natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Sd}T\cong\operatorname{Sd}(T^{\mathrm{op}})$. The last-vertex maps are weak equivalences by [lem-coef-subdivision-last-vertex-equivalence], giving $T\leftarrow\operatorname{Sd}T\cong\operatorname{Sd}(T^{\mathrm{op}})\to T^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products] to obtain the all-Kan zigzag $T\to\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}T\leftarrow\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}\operatorname{Sd}T\cong\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}\operatorname{Sd}(T^{\mathrm{op}})\to\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}(T^{\mathrm{op}})\leftarrow T^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its arrows are weak equivalences: the unit is one, and naturality of the unit and two-out-of-three in the model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] show that $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$ preserves weak equivalences. Combine this with the two pinch equivalences to obtain a natural zigzag of Kan weak equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}(z,x)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_D(x,z)$, also in the functor quasicategories.
The product compatibility needed for composition can be checked from the same cited statements. Put $R(T)=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}\operatorname{Sd}T$ and $E(T)=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}T$. Product projections give $R(S\times T)\to R(S)\times R(T)$, and the last-vertex maps give a commuting triangle from this map to $E(S)\times E(T)=E(S\times T)$. The direct arrow is a weak equivalence, since the last-vertex map is one and $E$ preserves weak equivalences as proved above. The arrow from $R(S)\times R(T)$ is also a weak equivalence: it is a product of weak equivalences between Kan complexes, hence factors as two pullbacks along Kan fibrations to a point, to which right properness applies. Two-out-of-three proves that the product comparison is a weak equivalence. The subdivision reversal respects these product projections degree by degree, and $E$ preserves products. Thus the natural opposite zigzags identify products as well as individual mapping spaces in the homotopy category of Kan complexes.
These comparisons respect composition: in the triangle spaces $V(a,b,d)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], reversal exchanges edges $01$ and $12$ and reverses $02$. Therefore it exchanges precomposition with postcomposition under the canonical composition classes. The calculation is by precomposition on every parameter simplex, so retains the associated higher homotopies. In particular the cone map becomes $u\mapsto\Delta_K(u)\alpha$ on the colimit boundary space $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(f,\Delta_Kz)$, and postcomposition by $p$ gives the specified base row.
For completeness reversal preserves weak equivalences: the degreewise formula $[\sigma,(t_0,\ldots,t_n)]\mapsto[\sigma,(t_n,\ldots,t_0)]$ gives a natural homeomorphism $|T^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|T|$, respecting the realization relations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] by the same operator conjugation formula. Reversal also identifies $P(u,v)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $P(v^{\mathrm{op}},u^{\mathrm{op}})$, by exchanging factors and interval endpoints, and preserves the constant-path comparison. Thus reversal, followed by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] along the all-Kan zigzags, preserves and reflects homotopy pullback tests. It takes the all-source test to the all-target test of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]; the quantifier over diagrams is unchanged because reversal is involutive. Applying the limit result to $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ proves exactly the colimit assertion and constant-target equivalence.

source.place: Opposite dual of Proposition 7.1.6.19; agent proof using the existing varying-boundary join-cone mapping formula.

proof.text: The comparison in step 1 is natural in the indexing simplicial set, the target quasicategory, and both cones by [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus]. For $L\to K$, precomposition restricts $f,g,\alpha,\beta$, sends a boundary transformation $a$ to $a|_L$, and leaves the apex maps $u$ unchanged. The identity $(a\beta)|_L=(a|_L)(\beta|_L)$, and the corresponding identity for $\alpha\Delta(u)$, identify the horizontal maps and their coherence paths with their restrictions. Postcomposition by $p$ commutes with each of these operations. The path-pullback maps apply these operations to all three entries, including the path; hence the apex identifications and the test comparisons commute naturally with them. The same calculation after the opposite construction gives colimit naturality. This is naturality of the comparisons between tests; it does not assert that a relative colimit or limit remains universal after changing its indexing shape.
